parsed.why: No criminalisation; state tolerates but polices public immodesty, blocks LGBT media, one advocacy group. Thin record: no documented trans-specific violence or targeting, but repressive state and no recourse, so silence is not safety.

No criminalisation and visible scene, but documented police targeting and abuse of trans women (forced bathing, extortion), 135+ harassment cases, high arrest rates; paper UPR acceptances unmatched by statute or remedy.

Bill jailing self-identification as trans up to three years with duty to report, awaiting assent; existing 'unnatural carnal knowledge' offence, mob justice, no recognition or protection, state-closed community infrastructure.

Safest: no criminalisation, high court voided bathroom exclusion and surgery requirement, tourist-tolerant. But no GI anti-discrimination statute, custody follows family register, gender-segregated bathing, and one documented detention of a trans activist among men.

No criminalisation and tolerant reputation, but legal recognition unimplemented so ID mismatches are routine, documented healthcare discrimination against trans women, no GI protections, 2025 Pride cancellations and surveillance of organisations signal narrowing.
